nodes.name: Run Time
nodes.notes: Runs EVERY day, Sundays included (design O-F). Sunday is decided by the Code: if the workflow does not run there is no summary, and that breaks INV-13. STAYS DISABLED until the delivery webhook and the daily watch exist.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Returns ONE row with the 6 keys as columns. If it returned one row per key, the whole workflow below would run 6 times — confirmed on 2026-09-07 in the reconnaissance run.

parameters.query:
-- Pivots into ONE SINGLE ROW on purpose. With one row per key, every node
-- below would run once per key: the first reconnaissance run brought the
-- patient list 6 times. The coalesce calls give sane defaults if a key
-- does not exist yet.
select
  coalesce(max(case when name = 'sends_max_seen'     then value end), '0')::bigint      as sends_max_seen,
  coalesce(max(case when name = 'price_marketing'    then value end), '0.0740')::numeric as price_marketing,
  coalesce(max(case when name = 'price_utility'      then value end), '0.0113')::numeric as price_utility,
  coalesce(max(case when name = 'anomaly_threshold'  then value end), '50')::int        as anomaly_threshold,
  coalesce(max(case when name = 'balance_margin'     then value end), '2.0')::numeric   as balance_margin,
  coalesce(max(case when name = 'account_restricted' then value end), 'false')          as account_restricted
from bot.config;

nodes.name: Gate A · Number
nodes.notes: Gate A: status CONNECTED, qualityRating != RED, and messagingLimit for gate B.

nodes.name: Gate A · Templates
nodes.notes: All three templates have to be APPROVED. One in PENDING cannot be used to send.

nodes.name: Firebase Token
nodes.notes: MISSING the credential: pick 'Client App - Firebase Key' in the Custom Auth dropdown. Returns idToken, which goes as a Bearer token in the next node.

nodes.name: Patients
nodes.notes: Paginated until exhausted: asks for page = $pageCount + 1 and stops when page >= totalPages. Confirmed on 2026-09-07: the API returns total, page, limit and totalPages. About 500 patients, i.e. 3 pages of 200. maxRequests 30 is a safety cap, not the stop mechanism.

nodes.name: Evaluate Gate A
nodes.notes: Gate A evaluated in a Code node and not in the IF conditions: it is 4 checks with readable reasons, and the concrete reason is what goes into the alert.

nodes.name: Channel Healthy?
nodes.notes: False branch = abort WITHOUT fetching patients and without writing anything. It is INV-8, and it is cheap because it cuts before the expensive part.

nodes.name: Channel Down Alert
nodes.notes: INV-15: no parse_mode. INV-13: aborting is a signal too, not a silence. | INV-15 (corrected 2026-09-08): parse_mode has NO 'None' option and omitting it does NOT disable parsing - n8n sends Markdown anyway, and a key with an odd number of underscores kills the alert with a 400. HTML is set explicitly and & < > are escaped in every interpolation.

nodes.name: Compute Candidates
nodes.notes: On Sunday it returns an empty list but the workflow carries on, so the summary goes out anyway (design O-F). If the Schedule skipped Sundays, a Sunday without a message would be indistinguishable from n8n being down.

nodes.name: Existing Keys
nodes.notes: First anti-duplicate layer (design O-A). It is not redundant with the sender's ON CONFLICT: if this filter fails, the candidate count is inflated and the gates decide on false numbers.

parameters.query: select unique_key from bot.sends where unique_key = any($1);

nodes.name: Last Templates
nodes.notes: Alternation by the template ACTUALLY used, not by counting rows (spec 4.6). The old SATELLITE design counted records and the cleanup reset the count: a patient who renewed got the same message twice.

parameters.query:
select distinct on (patient_id) patient_id, template
from bot.sends
where milestone = '20' and patient_id = any($1)
order by patient_id, created_at desc;

nodes.name: Marketing Opt-outs
nodes.notes: A single call for everyone, not one per patient. Spec 4.6 point 2: the opt-out is checked BEFORE picking the template, not after the send fails.

nodes.name: Table Health
nodes.notes: Compared against sends_max_seen (design D-E). Detects a shrunken table, which also covers restoring an old backup: the INV-17 scenario.

parameters.query: select count(*)::bigint as total from bot.sends;

nodes.name: Balance
nodes.notes: YCloud charges against prepaid credit. Zero balance = every send fails = burned keys. That is why it is checked BEFOREHAND (spec 7.1).

nodes.name: Gate B Alert
nodes.notes: INV-15 (corrected 2026-09-08): parse_mode has NO 'None' option and omitting it does NOT disable parsing - n8n sends Markdown anyway, and a key with an odd number of underscores kills the alert with a 400. HTML is set explicitly and & < > are escaped in every interpolation.

nodes.name: Any Candidates?
nodes.notes: Zero candidates is NOT a failure: it is the normal case most days. But the summary goes out anyway (INV-13), which is why the false branch goes to the summary and not into the void.

nodes.name: One By One
nodes.notes: Batch size 1: one sub-workflow execution per patient. Replaces the mode:each of the Execute Sub-workflow node, which is deprecated. CAREFUL: output 0 = 'done', output 1 = 'loop'.

nodes.name: Send To One Patient
nodes.notes: The only workflow that sends. The 7 fields are the frozen contract of the send sub-workflow.

nodes.name: Watermark
nodes.notes: AFTER the sends and with greatest(). Before them it would leave the mark at the count prior to today's keys, and tomorrow the guard would compare against a number lower than the real one. greatest() makes it idempotent and safe against an aborted run.

nodes.name: Notify Summary
nodes.notes: INV-15: no parse_mode. INV-13: this message goes out every day, even when the result is zero. | INV-15 (corrected 2026-09-08): parse_mode has NO 'None' option and omitting it does NOT disable parsing - n8n sends Markdown anyway, and a key with an odd number of underscores kills the alert with a 400. HTML is set explicitly and & < > are escaped in every interpolation.
